what_happened: The person running Athena wrote the acceptance for job sz3z as "run `athena plan` on this repository's real queue". The producer works in a one-commit copy with no records/ directory, so it cannot do that. The same error was made hours earlier for job e5sg. The fix that would give agents an evidence snapshot (d103) is still held and has not landed. The person running Athena caught the error and logged it as a repeat mistake.
cause: Acceptance criteria are written with no defined list of what the producer and verifier can see and run (a one-commit working copy, no records/, only the diff, snapshot and check output). Nothing compares a criterion's required evidence with that list, so a criterion needing unreachable data looks valid. The earlier lesson lives only in the logged case and in the held fix, not where the criterion writer is made to look. So the same kind of criterion was written again.
prevention: A check at request and reading admission that scans each acceptance criterion for evidence the agents cannot reach (real records/, the real queue, running athena commands against live state). It would refuse or hold such a criterion, naming the visible-evidence list, until the criterion is rewritten against a fixture or the evidence snapshot. Landing the held d103 snapshot would make real-queue evidence available. The visible-evidence list should also be shown to whoever writes acceptance.
proposed_request: Add an admission check that rejects any acceptance criterion in a request or accepted reading that requires evidence the producer or verifier cannot see. The agents work in a one-commit copy with no records/ directory, and see only the diff, the snapshot and check output. The check should flag criteria that require running athena commands such as `athena plan` or `athena status` on the real queue or real records, or that read records/ or other state-directory data. When it flags one, it should say what the agents can see and suggest a fixture-based criterion, or one that depends on the evidence snapshot job d103 once that lands. Show the visible-evidence list to the criterion writer in the request guidance. Acceptance: (1) a request whose criterion says to run `athena plan` on the real queue is held with a message naming the unreachable evidence; (2) the same criterion rewritten against a test fixture is admitted; (3) replaying the check over past real requests gives a false-hold rate reported in the job output; (4) sz3z and e5sg style criteria are both caught.
